notes: Carpenters: 2.6x a farm laborer's spring rate (village, 1802-04) and 4.7x Kyoto's unskilled wage (Osaka carpenters), times the 13-sen unskilled day. Carpenters only; other crafts unmeasured.

A carpenter's winning bid of over 30 ryo (Shibasaki, Tama, 1841) for a new 6-shaku-bay sanctuary with a cusped gable; carvings, timber and village labor outside it. 30 ryo is ~2,000 Kyoto laborer-days (0255's arithmetic) = ~26 koku at 13 sen; scaled to a 4.2-shaku plain bay by roof area (0.49) to width (0.7): 12.7-18.2 koku. A repair of a sanctuary this size (Mitake, 1764-70) cost ~9.5 ryo, so a new build above that fits. Carpenter-days for a new build: SILENT.

The box without food: 25-35 monme a bay (1803), seven to a box, 3.6-5 monme a head = 4-5.4 Kyoto laborer-days (0266's arithmetic at 0.92). Food SILENT. Late shogunate 40-60 monme a bay.

A Kaifeng village troupe: no more than ten-odd thousand cash for three days (undated), ~1.7-3.3 koku at the 1736 laborer's 75 cash = 13 sen. A big bought-in troupe for a market town's festival ran far more (Hamanoichi, Funai, 1690-1737: 839-6,530 monme a run, 43 players; the fee is the historian's hypothesis). Most village plays were the young men's own.
0266: no fee for a hired musician.

A pair of stone lanterns contracted with Chugoro of Atsugi for 4 ryo 3 bu, Shibasaki 1841, delivered to Hachioji Shinmachi; size not given (0269). ~310 laborer-days (0269's arithmetic). A ryo is 60 monme (0255's rate), ~65 Kyoto laborer-days at 0.92 monme (1802-04), so ~0.85 koku at our 13-sen day.

A village worship hall: 11 ryo 2 bu to the carpenter for raising it and its joinery, woodcutters and sawyers included, one sum, Shibasaki 1840 (0268/0255); size not given. ~9.8 koku; scaled like the sanctuary (0.49-0.7, a 6-shaku shrine's buildings to our 4.2-shaku one): 4.8-6.9. Its ratio to the same carpenter's sanctuary bid (0.38) matches the catalog's pavilion-to-sanctuary ratio. A ryo is 60 monme (0255's rate), ~65 Kyoto laborer-days at 0.92 monme (1802-04), so ~0.85 koku at our 13-sen day.
